content.title: What is the NIO Package?
content.description: NIO (New Input/Output) is an enhanced I/O API introduced in Java to provide faster, scalable, and more flexible file and network operations using buffers, channels, and paths.

content.content: The java.nio package was introduced to overcome the limitations of traditional Java I/O. Unlike the older java.io package, NIO uses buffers, channels, and the Files API to efficiently process large amounts of data, making it ideal for high-performance applications.

content.title: Why Learn NIO?
content.content: NIO provides faster file operations, better scalability, efficient memory usage, and improved support for large files and network programming.
The NIO package is built around four important concepts: Buffers, Channels, Paths, and the Files utility class.

rows: Stores data temporarily during I/O operations.
Transfers data between buffers and files.
Provides utility methods for file operations.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Unlike java.io streams, NIO transfers data through buffers connected to channels.

content.content: A Buffer is a temporary memory area used to hold data while it is being transferred. Java provides several buffer types, including ByteBuffer, CharBuffer, IntBuffer, and FloatBuffer.

content.title: ByteBuffer Example

content.content: A Channel represents a connection to a file, socket, or other I/O device. Data is transferred between the channel and a buffer.

content.title: FileChannel Example
Performance Advantage
content.content: Channels can support faster I/O operations because they work directly with buffers and may use operating system optimizations.
The Path interface represents file and directory locations. It replaces many uses of the older File class.

content.title: Creating a Path

content.content: The Files utility class provides convenient static methods for creating, copying, moving, deleting, and reading files.

items.question: Files.copy()
items.answer: Copies a file from one location to another.

items.question: Files.readString()
items.answer: Reads the complete contents of a text file into a String.

items.question: Large File Processing
items.answer: Read and write large files efficiently.

items.question: Web Servers
items.answer: Handle thousands of client connections using non-blocking I/O.

items.question: Database Systems
items.answer: Efficiently transfer data between storage and memory.

items.question: Cloud Applications
items.answer: Process files with high performance and scalability.

content.title: Warehouse Conveyor Belt
content.content: Traditional I/O is like workers carrying one box at a time. NIO is like using conveyor belts and storage bins, allowing many items to move efficiently with less effort.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers often ask about the differences between java.io and java.nio, the purpose of buffers and channels, the Files API, Path interface, and the advantages of non-blocking I/O.

items.question: Can data be transferred directly through a Channel?
items.answer: No. Channels exchange data through buffers.

items.question: Should Path replace File everywhere?
items.answer: For modern Java applications, Path and Files are generally preferred over File.

items.question: What happens if flip() is not called on a ByteBuffer?
items.answer: The buffer remains in write mode, making it impossible to read the stored data correctly.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: NIO is built around Buffers, Channels, Paths, and Files, providing a faster and more flexible alternative to traditional Java I/O.
